content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. Type checking shows no errors in it.

- **`byId`** uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit`.
- **`totalAge`** uses `sumBy` from `es-toolkit`, with a callback `(row) => row.age` instead of the lodash `'age'` shorthand, which the strict version doesn't accept.
- **`isBlank`** uses `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The strict package has no `isEmpty`, and compat follows lodash's behaviour for the whole input range (null, booleans, numbers, strings, arrays and objects).

The exported function signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged. There are no hand-written replacements and no adapter.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 606 bytes (min+gzip) and 95 bytes of own code. Importing all three from `es-toolkit/compat` instead came to 3404 bytes (min+gzip) and 98 bytes of own code. Mixing strict and compat is therefore the smaller option.

I couldn't measure the original or compare results against it. `lodash` isn't installed, so `src/module.ts` fails to build and type-check. I also didn't run the migrated functions against example inputs. I checked behaviour only by reading the library's API.
